beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:storytelling, growing wonder]In {1992|nineteen ninety-two}, in eastern ^China, villagers pumped the water out of a pond, and found a hall the size of a ^cathedral, cut by ^hand into solid rock.
[d:tension][act:the kicker, quietly amazed]Then they found ^twenty-three more.

[d:calm][p:0.93][act:touring the space, awed][tune:level]^Floors of up to thirteen hundred square metres: about ^three basketball courts. [act:looking up][tune:level]^Roofs up to eighteen metres high, as tall as a ^six-storey building, sloping with the ^rock layers. [act:a quick inventory][tune:fall]^Pillars, ^stairs, ^drainage.
[d:build][go:2|0][act:close up, admiring]And ^every surface is covered in neat bands of ^chisel marks, about half a metre apart: the signature of ^hand work, blow after blow.

[d:build][act:precise, intrigued]Neighbouring caverns are separated by walls just ^half a metre thick: less than an arm's ^length. [act:quiet emphasis][tune:fall]Not ^one breaks through. [p:0.9][act:marvelling, slower]Imagine carving that close@adj to a hall you can't ^see, without ever breaking ^in.
[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:hushed, the real puzzle]And there's not a ^single record@noun of who dug them, or ^why. [act:quiet wonder]A project@noun this huge, and history never wrote it ^down.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:a solid clue, steady]Inside, pottery was found from the ^Western Han dynasty, which ruled China about two ^thousand years ago. [act:the everyday picture, light]Pots are dated by ^style: like cars, they changed fashion over time, and an expert can tell the era at a ^glance.

[d:aside][act:a careful caveat, lighter][tune:fallrise]But that dates when the ^pots arrived. [act:pointed, simple][tune:fall]Not the ^digging. [gap:0.4][p:0.93][act:the everyday picture, clear]It's like finding an old ^newspaper in an attic. [p:0.9][act:landing it, slow]It shows the house@noun was standing by ^then, but it could be far ^older.

[d:reveal][p:0.93][act:opening the options, lively]The engineers who studied the caves list ^seven possibilities. [act:counting them off, brisk][tune:level]^Quarries, tombs, storage, a retreat, a secret army camp, a place of sacrifice, or even a ^palace.

[d:build][sfx:hit][act:practical, weighing it]Quarrying is the ^simplest: soft, even ^siltstone, fine silt turned to stone, with a river right beside it, a ready-made road for heavy ^blocks. [act:the catch, even][tune:fall]But ^nobody has traced the stone to a ^building.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Dug as ^quarries? [act:the verdict, honest][tune:fall]^*Open question*. [act:fair, with a reservation][tune:fallrise]The simplest answer, still ^unconfirmed. [act:naming the test, practical]Match the stone to a ^building, or date the ^digging itself, and it could finally be ^settled.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:warm, admiring, the last word]Two thousand years of ^silence, carved with remarkable ^care.
